scope: Proposition 5.5 of the manuscript “Finite Smith–Toda Complexes at Varying Primes” (preprints/Finite-Smith-Toda-Complexes-at-Varying-Primes-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 308 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 13dce3978089a78f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 24-25. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the chosen cycles through ba, there exist the following data as germs along U: 1. Filtered Λ-graded commutative ring spectra Ra p, with an equivalence Ra ≃ hΛ(Ra p) at every filtration order, compatible with the filtered algebra structures. 2. Maps of whole unfiltered graded commutative algebras Ra p → S(p), where the sphere is constant in the weight grading, together with a homotopy identifying their normalized evaluation with Equation (5.1). 24 3. Filtered finite-cell Ra p-modules Ka p , with an equivalence Ka ≃ hΛ(Ka p ) of filtered modules. The algebra models, their comparisons, and the evaluation homotopies may be chosen relative to the preceding stage. Thus the maps Ra−1 → Ra and Ra−1 p → Ra p and their evaluations form compatible diagrams of algebras. No algebra structure is required on Ka p .
